title: October 12 pensioners’ march (episode ownership pending)

organizer: Independent Telegram channels called for a Belarus-wide pensioners’ march; no named organization established.
participants_original: Several thousand older participants in Minsk; additional actions elsewhere uncounted.
threshold_50_evidence: The same-day report explicitly characterizes attendance in Minsk as several thousand people, which supports at least 50 at that one gathering without relying on arrests or adding other cities.

start_date.summary: Same-day live report dates the march to 12 October 2020.

end_date.summary: The chronology reports the march ending that evening as participants dispersed; no later date is inferred.

location.summary: Minsk march follows named central avenues/squares; separate marches also described in Brest, Grodno, Gomel and other cities.

scope.summary: The call is described as countrywide and several cities are documented, but linked local-vs-national unit ownership remains for review.

organizer.summary: Independent Telegram channels called for pensioners’ marches; no more specific organizing body is established.

title: October 25 People’s Ultimatum march
location: Minsk; actions elsewhere in Belarus reported without individual city detail or counts.
scope: Nationally coordinated political action: the report links the Minsk march and nationwide actions to the opposition leader’s countrywide ultimatum. Participant evidence applies only to Minsk.
organizer: Opposition movement under Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya’s People’s Ultimatum; report identifies the ultimatum but not local event committees.
participants_original: Tens of thousands in Minsk according to eyewitness-based reporting; some estimates were higher than 100,000. No city-level numbers for other locations.
threshold_50_evidence: The same-day report describes tens of thousands at the Minsk march itself, clearly exceeding 50. This is qualitative and eyewitness-attributed; no exact lower bound is manufactured and no countrywide estimate is aggregated.

start_date.summary: Same-day report dates the People’s Ultimatum march to 25 October.

end_date.summary: No event ending date is reported; leave unknown.

location.summary: Minsk gathering reported with additional nationwide actions, but no other city names or counts.

scope.summary: The national opposition ultimatum was to prompt people across the country to act; same-day report says protests occurred across the country. Minsk attendance estimate belongs only to Minsk.

organizer.summary: Action was identified with the opposition leader’s national ultimatum; no local organizer named.

demands.summary: Ultimatum calls for Lukashenko to leave, an end to street violence, and release of political prisoners.

participants_original.summary: Eyewitness-based report gives tens of thousands in Minsk and some higher estimates; no exact number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative tens-of-thousands description at the Minsk march supports >=50 at that gathering.

state_response.summary: Flash grenades and rubber bullets reported; code dispersal and shooting only as described, while arrests, beatings and killings remain unknown.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence established in this short report.

episode_ownership.summary: A separate dated national ultimatum rally is described; the broader August-onset movement continues, but this event is organized around a distinct 25 October deadline. Review onset/episode linkage before counting.

notes: Potential separate day-specific gathering tied to a distinct ultimatum deadline; ongoing election protest wave began earlier. Do not combine the daily rally with the next day’s announced strike absent evidence of continuous public gathering. Official MM baseline, schema and ccode mapping remain unverified.
open_questions: Independent reviewer should confirm the action is distinct from the ongoing post-election protest campaign and onset belongs to 25 October.
Check next-day worker/student activity separately for actual public gathering, at least 50 simultaneous participants and a domestic-state demand.
Check November and December for continuity or a distinct continuation; do not transfer this gathering’s attendance.

title: October 26 Minsk pensioner/student march supporting striking workers
location: Minsk: the report describes assembly near the Red Church/Independence Square and a march through central Minsk. Other locations are described separately and not pooled.
scope: Minsk gathering; separate actions are reported in other towns, but no common national event/count is inferred from their shared date.
organizer: No named local organizer; a recurring pensioners’ march was joined by students on the day of the announced strike.
participants_original: Thousands of pensioners and students in the shared Minsk march; a five-thousand estimate for the column at 15:06 is attributed by Charter97 to Nasha Niva.
threshold_50_evidence: Charter97’s live report describes thousands at the Minsk march and attributes a contemporaneous five-thousand column estimate to Nasha Niva. This clearly exceeds 50 at the Minsk gathering; do not add other city marches.

start_date.summary: Page dates the student protests and march to 26 October.

end_date.summary: Live updates report the march ending and participants dispersing at 16:42 on 26 October.

location.summary: Begins near Red Church/Independence Square and follows central avenues; other towns are separate.

scope.summary: The recorded attendance is for a shared Minsk pensioner/student march; other-city marches are reported separately.

organizer.summary: Traditional pensioners’ action with student participation; no named local organizer.

participants_original.summary: Thousands of pensioners and students in Minsk; the specific five-thousand column estimate is attributed to Nasha Niva by Charter97.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Contemporaneous live coverage describes thousands at one Minsk column, clearly above 50; no multi-city total used.

demands.summary: Support for strike and calls for Interior Minister accountability constitute demands on the Belarusian state.

state_response.summary: The caption reports approximately 200 detentions that day but does not link them specifically to this march; candidate-specific response remains unknown.

episode_ownership.summary: October 26 march was timed to the failed ultimatum and national-strike start and is physically dated separately from Oct25; link to the larger movement still needs independent episode review.

notes: This is a distinct dated street march on Oct 26, separate from the Oct25 People’s Ultimatum rally; it supported striking workers and the day’s national-strike call. No source here establishes that factory walkouts themselves were public gatherings. The five-thousand point estimate is second-hand within Charter97; the broader qualitative thousands statement comes from Charter97 live coverage.
open_questions: Scientific reviewer should assess whether the Oct26 action is a distinct episode/onset versus continuation of the August-onset movement; its separate date, event setting and strike-related call support but do not settle this.
Worker strikes at plants are excluded from this march unless a separate public street gathering with threshold and demand is established.
Search adjacent months for related movement continuity without transferring this attendance.
